intro.title: Frontend Performance & Core Web Vitals
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple web page that measures and displays key performance metrics known as Core Web Vitals, such as Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) and Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS). You'll learn how to use the PerformanceObserver API in JavaScript to capture these real-time metrics from the browser. The main technologies involved are vanilla JavaScript, HTML for structure, and the browser's built-in performance monitoring tools. By the end, you'll understand how to implement basic performance tracking to improve user experience on your own websites.
intro.usecase: Core Web Vitals directly impact user experience in high-traffic applications like e-commerce product pages, news article feeds, and banking dashboards. Developers optimize Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) to ensure hero images load instantly on retail sites, improve First Input Delay (FID) for responsive search filters on travel booking platforms, and minimize Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) to prevent checkout buttons from moving during payment flows. These metrics are monitored in tools like Google Search Console and directly influence SEO rankings and conversion rates, making performance optimization a critical business requirement rather than just a technical concern.
